All exact doctor trials must pass below 180 seconds and nearest-rank p95 must be at most 135 seconds on both pinned runtimes.

adverse_evidence: All twelve candidate exact-doctor trials failed: 0/6 passed on Python 3.14.4 and 0/6 passed on Python 3.12.13.
Candidate nearest-rank p95 was 187.051918 seconds on Python 3.14.4 and 187.290851 seconds on Python 3.12.13, above the 135-second promotion limit.
Neither candidate runtime completed below the unchanged 180-second internal timeout.
The candidate did not reproduce the complete frozen 381-execution behavior vector through the required exact doctor command.
Full .autopilot test discovery and full repository CI were not run after the decisive two-runtime fail-closed result.
The candidate's p95 changed in mixed directions relative to baseline: 1.279431 seconds lower on Python 3.14 and 0.344942 seconds higher on Python 3.12; this is not consistent superiority evidence.
dissent_preserved: The focused contract, seed-isolation, fixture-isolation, and healing tests passed, so rejection of promotion is not a finding that every isolation property failed.
The Python 3.14 p95 is slightly lower than its baseline p95, but all trials still failed and the result is far above the promotion threshold.
The baseline court recorded fixture construction as a hypothesis only; this experiment does not establish it as the dominant runtime cause.
A content-addressed fixture may remain useful outside this promotion claim, but usefulness cannot substitute for the sealed end-to-end burden.
